materials.name: Yellow embossed wallpaper
materials.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless physically based BASE COLOR texture for wallpaper in a first-person Backrooms-style game. Create one square full-bleed texture swatch viewed perfectly straight on, orthographic, of old pale mustard-yellow embossed vinyl wallpaper found in an empty late-1970s office. Fine, restrained vertical meandering pinstripes with tiny elongated diamond / leaf shapes, each only a few centimeters wide in the real material, densely repeating across the swatch. A subtle tactile paper grain and very slight age discoloration; predominantly yellow ochre and straw yellow, with the embossed pattern only slightly darker. The whole swatch represents about 1 meter by 1 meter. It should read as essentially yellow wallpaper at room-view distance, with the woven print visible close up. Natural photographic material detail, subdued pattern contrast, no plaster/concrete patches, no cracks or peeling. BASE COLOR ONLY: diffuse neutral uniform frontal illumination, no directional light or shading, no ambient occlusion, no shadows, no specular highlights, no vignetting, no blur, no fog, no grey veil. Seamlessly repeatable on left/right and top/bottom edges, consistent density across edges, no obvious center motif. Texture fills the entire image edge to edge, no borders, room, architecture, objects, text, symbols, watermark or labels. Output a high-detail square raster texture.

materials.name: Beige office carpet
materials.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless BASE COLOR texture for beige wall-to-wall office carpet in a first-person Backrooms-style game. Create a square full-bleed overhead orthographic macro photograph of plain short dense cut-pile commercial carpet, the type covering empty late-1970s office floors. Sandy beige, light camel, muted golden tan fibers. Soft irregular fine pile, tightly packed wool/nylon fibers, with subtle natural variation and a few faint wear marks, no large stains. The entire image represents 1 meter by 1 meter of carpet. Realistic individual fine fiber detail at close range; at a distance it must read as a quiet even beige carpet, not tiles, woven fabric, a rug, checkerboard, stripes, braids, stitching or a geometric pattern. Color is warm beige, not gray, green or orange. BASE COLOR ONLY: neutral, completely even diffuse lighting, no directional shadows, no ambient occlusion, no highlights, no baked shading, no depth of field, no fog or vignetting. Perfectly flat view, consistent detail scale, seamlessly repeatable on all four edges. No room, furniture, edges of a rug, border, objects, text, watermark or labels.

materials.name: Warm fine cast concrete
materials.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: one seamless PBR BASE COLOR texture for cast-concrete pedestals in a first-person Backrooms puzzle game. Primary request: a square, full-bleed, perfectly orthographic photograph of fine smooth cast architectural microconcrete, warm light limestone-beige grey. Represents exactly 0.8 meter by 0.8 meter of real material. Quiet subtle cloudy mineral variation, fine cement grain and sparsely distributed tiny pinhole pores about 0.2 to 1.2 millimeters across; solid cast stone with a matte unpolished finish, delicately visible small details up close but calm uniform material from a distance. Main color warm greige around sRGB #b8b3a3, naturally restrained low contrast, with no yellow ochre tint. No big holes, coarse stones, large aggregate, terrazzo, marble veins, brush strokes, trowel ridges, seams, formwork lines, cracks, scratches, damage, large stains, repeating motifs or directional grain. Uniform flat neutral diffuse frontal illumination, BASE COLOR ONLY, no baked directional shading, no ambient occlusion, shadows, highlights, gradients, vignette or blur. Seamlessly tileable at every edge. Texture fills image edge to edge. No actual pedestal, room, shapes, objects, frame, text, watermark, labels, grid or multiple panels. High resolution detailed square raster.

materials.name: Fine-fissured mineral-fiber office ceiling panel
materials.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless PBR BASE COLOR texture for a single typical suspended office acoustic ceiling panel in a first-person Backrooms game. A square full-bleed perfectly orthographic straight-on photograph of the face of a conventional fine-fissured mineral-fiber acoustic ceiling board, the classic plain inexpensive office ceiling material. The entire swatch represents exactly 65 centimeters by 65 centimeters of a real panel. Dense fine chalky mineral fibers, irregular small pinhole pores and many characteristic short thin naturally branching elongated fissures distributed organically in different directions, about 2 to 12 mm long and less than 1 mm wide, with quieter areas between them. Dry matte porous painted mineral fiber, realistic tactile detail, soft warm ivory/off-white around sRGB #ded8bc to match a warm yellow-wallpaper beige-carpet office interior. Fissures should be visibly darker warm grey-beige and read clearly as tiny acoustic pores at close distance, not gigantic cracks. Uniform density, natural nonrepeating arrangement without any dominant motif. BASE COLOR ONLY: completely even neutral diffuse illumination, no directional light, shadows, ambient occlusion, highlights, gradients, vignetting or blur. Seamless tileable edges, edge-to-edge material detail, no panel border, no metal grid, no square pattern, no beveled frame, no seams, no actual room, ceiling scene, perspective, objects, text, labels, watermark or multiple images. No concrete mottling, marble, wood, carpet fibers or large stains. High resolution square raster material photograph.
materials.grid: 24 mm warm greige T-grid (#c9c0ae), slightly darker than the panel, composited at startup in src/materials.ts; same 65 cm grid as square pedestal width, fixtures and pedestal placement

rendering.style_preserved: Original Backrooms wallpaper and carpet, original warm palette and physical scale

normal_maps.source: Estimated from fine Sobel gradients of the existing albedo in src/material-detail.ts
normal_maps.wrapping: Mirrored repeat with corrected tangent normal signs

roughness_maps.source: Estimated from existing albedo at startup

rendering.carpet_finish: MeshPhysicalMaterial sheen 0.25, sheen roughness 0.95; contact shading includes the sheen contribution

concrete_pedestals.finish: Matte fine cast concrete, 0.8 m per tile, JPG base color with estimated linear normal and roughness maps; matching bowls, sharp edges without bevels, original dimensions retained
concrete_pedestals.tint: Material color multiplies the texture by target / measured texture mean in linear RGB, preserving the original beige palette and pore variation

rendering.lamp_diffuser: Procedural 512² opal/prismatic diffuser within the existing ceiling fixture
rendering.panel_light: 9 probes per 62.6 cm diffuser filling the opening in a 24 mm T-grid, within a 65 cm ceiling tile; shared dimensions for visible fixtures, lighting bake and PMREM; 55% static diffuse plus 45% live spotlight contribution
rendering.bounce_light: One coarse Lambertian reflection from floor and walls, with room/pedestal visibility; mean material colors

room_lightmaps.calculation: At startup in the existing lighting worker; no per-frame bake

billiard_balls.material: Opaque polished resin, MeshPhysicalMaterial; original red/blue hues and 8 cm diameter
billiard_balls.polish_map: Shared procedural linear roughness texture, 256 squared, mipmapped and anisotropic; no color grain or painted highlights
billiard_balls.contact_shadow: Occupied cups analytically occlude their baked panel illumination with the 4 cm sphere and a panel-sized penumbra; gap-based contact occlusion attenuates indirect and reflected light. A streamed byte attribute changes immediately on pick/place; empty cup color stays uniform.
billiard_balls.reflections: Separate sharp 256-pixel PMREM captured once from the real textured, lit starting room at ball height after materials/light preparation; HDR diffusers included, balls and portal images excluded; shared local approximation without live cube cameras

rendering.environment: Shared soft 128-pixel PMREM for architecture in src/room-environment.ts; sharp 256-pixel actual-scene probe for polished balls in src/scene.ts; both prepared once at startup
